newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney's gay mardi gras wins major corporate support.
newsitem.headline: Sydney's gay mardi gras wins major corporate support.

text.p: Sydney's Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras has a soft spot for a frock, so it is only fitting that a frock shop, albeit one of Australia's major department stores, should become the latest sponsor of the homosexual parade.
In announcing the 1997 homosexual parade, organisers on Thursday said total sponsorship now amounted to about A$200,000 (US$158,000), compared with about A$40,000 in 1992.
Mardi Gras president Bev Lange said many mainstream companies were now prepared to back the homosexual parade, which was once a protest march for gay rights.
"A couple of years ago not many major corporations felt comfortable enough being associated with a gay and lesbian organisation," said Mardi Gras president Bev Lange.
"But with organisations like Telstra supporting the Mardi Gras and not losing any of their market share, this has shown other corporations you can be a supporter."
Australia's international airline Qantas Airways began sponsoring the event in 1995, with telecommunications carrier Telstra signing up last year.

Family department store Grace Bros has become the latest corporate backer, agreeing to sponsor the post-parade party called the Sleaze Ball and entering into a deal to sell Mardi Gras merchandise, ranging from t-shirts to tea towels.
The value of the store's sponsorship was not revealed.
A Grace Bros spokeswoman said the store felt it should "support such high-profile business generating events for sound commercial reasons".

Sydney's Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras started as a protest march 18 years ago, but has grown into the month-long festival of homosexual pride, culminating in a gay parade that last year attracted 600,000 spectators.

The 1997 festival, from January 31 to March 1, was also expected to attract more than 5,000 international visitors. The festival injects more than A$58 million a year into the local economy, according to a study by the Australian Graduate School of Management.
